leads.claim: The Air Force lacks authentic physical evidence to confirm the interplanetary theory regarding flying saucers.
leads.why: A high-ranking Air Force official explicitly addresses the status of physical evidence in the context of UAP investigations.
leads.government_response: The Air Force officially neither accepts nor rejects the interplanetary theory due to a lack of indisputable physical evidence.
leads.quote: we have no authen-tic physical evidence that they are interplanetary.

leads.claim: An Air Force official denied possessing any parts of flying saucers or having seen occupants.
leads.why: The statement directly addresses the custody of physical material and biological entities.
leads.government_response: The official denied possession of any parts or sightings of occupants.
leads.quote: stated that he had no parts of flying saucers in his possession at present.

leads.claim: A substance touched by a policeman dissolved upon contact, leaving a sticky residue.
leads.why: Describes a specific physical interaction with an unidentified material, though the origin is not confirmed as UAP-related.
leads.material_description: A substance that dissolved and left a sticky odorless residue.
leads.quote: the portion he handled dissolved at once, leaving a sticky odorless residue.

leads.claim: A saucer crashed near Denver, Colorado, with three little men discovered inside.
leads.why: Reports a specific recovery claim of biological entities, though the government explicitly denies the event.
leads.government_response: The Defense Department repeated its denial of flying saucers.
leads.quote: three little men had been discovered inside it.

doc_verdict: The document contains no evidence of obtained UAP material; it consists of press clippings and official statements where the Air Force consistently denies possessing physical evidence or biological entities.
